name.text: Integration by substitution of definite Integral

questiontext.text:
Evaluate by the use of substitution method:
\(\displaystyle\int_{{@lower@}}^{{@upper@}} {@f_x@} dx =\) [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

Find \(\displaystyle\int_{{@lower@}}^{{@upper@}} {@f_x@} dx\) by use of substitution method.

We recall that the antiderivative of \(\displaystyle u^{n}\) is \(\displaystyle \frac{u^{n+1}}{n+1}\) where \(\displaystyle n \neq -1\).

Let \(u= {@us@}\). Then \(du={@diff_u@} \, dx \). So \( \displaystyle dx = \frac{du}{{@diff_u@}} \).

When \( x \rightarrow {@lower@}, u \rightarrow {@lower_u@} \).

When \( x \rightarrow {@upper@}, u \rightarrow {@upper_u@} \).

By substituting the values of \(x\) by their corresponding values of \(u\), and also \( dx\) by \( \frac{du}{{@diff_u@}} \) in the original integral, we get;

\( \begin{align} \displaystyle \int_{{@lower@}}^{{@upper@}} {@f_x@} dx & = \int_{{@lower_u@}}^{{@upper_u@}} \frac{@constant@}{{@diff_u*u^power@}} \, du \\ & = \left[ {@expr2@} \right]_{{@lower_u@}}^{{@upper_u@}} \\ & = {@ta_1@} \end{align} \)
